$comment: THE COMMITTED HALF OF THE ORACLE'S HONESTY. Two declarations live here because both are human
judgements and both belong in review rather than in code.
`formats` says, for every format this library generates, either who independently graded it or
why nobody did. It is RECONCILED against the set of formats the library actually generates,
which scripts/oracle/formats.ts derives by running the generators themselves. A generated
format missing from this object FAILS the run, and an entry here for a format the library does
not generate fails it too. Neither side can drift quietly.
`corpus` is the declared seed corpus: every artifact the validator is asked about, named by
generator kind and by the seed that regenerates it byte-identically. Adding `excluded` to an
entry takes it out of the graded set and publishes the artifact and the reason in the coverage
declaration; the gate then refuses to count it toward the pass. That is the ONLY way to make
the graded set smaller. There is no way at all to make a validator finding smaller: no severity
downgrade, no warning-only mode, no suppression list.
The profile each artifact is graded against is NOT written here. It is read off the generated
resource's own meta.profile, so the two cannot drift.

fhir.gradedAgainst: the US Core 6.1.0 package (hl7.fhir.us.core 6.1.0) on FHIR R4 4.0.1

hl7v2.reason: No public, file-based, offline HL7 v2 validator was found. The NIST validation-tool project publishes no README, no command-line entry point and no documented file input, and the tool itself is hosted, so a verdict from it would be reproducible by rerunning a service rather than from a seed. HL7 v2 output therefore carries only the sibling parser's round-trip, which is not an independent verdict.

ccda.reason: The ONC reference C-CDA validator is server-shaped: a Tomcat 8.5 web archive on Java 8, needing 4GB or more of memory, driven over an HTTP form-data API, and it ships none of the externally published code systems and value sets it depends on. C-CDA output therefore carries only the sibling parser's round-trip, which is not an independent verdict.

x12.reason: No public, file-based validator for X12 005010 was found, so nothing independent has graded this output. It carries only the sibling parser's round-trip, which is not an independent verdict.
